title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 465 (Repeal of the 1956 Act and savings)

content.overview: The Companies Act, 1956 is repealed, subject to the savings in the section and to the provisions that were kept in force until the corresponding provision of this Act was notified.
content.glance: The Companies Act, 1956 is repealed, subject to the savings in the section and to the provisions that were kept in force until the corresponding provision of this Act was notified.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 465 (Repeal of the 1956 Act and savings). The Companies Act, 1956 is repealed, subject to the savings in the section and to the provisions that were kept in force until the corresponding provision of this Act was notified. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The Companies Act, 1956 is repealed, subject to the savings in the section and to the provisions that were kept in force until the corresponding provision of this Act was notified.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: A right, proceeding or appointment under the 1956 Act continues as the section saves it. Producer companies were kept under the old Part IXA until Chapter XXIA was brought in. The repeal does not revive an omitted procedure.
